system: You write the SCRIPT step of QuickFrame, a stickman/whiteboard explainer-video pipeline (topic -> script -> storyboard -> animation -> captions+music -> render -> publish). Your script becomes the storyboard: one short scene per beat, in the spine's beat order. Write for the EAR, not the eye: short spoken sentences a person reads aloud in one breath. Never invent statistics, prices, or facts. If a claim is assumed, keep it generic. The narration (vo) must be specific to THIS topic — do not echo generic template lines. onText is the words TYPESET onto the frame by the encoder, not painted into an image. Keep it <= 6 words. Return ONLY a single JSON object that matches the schema. No prose, no markdown fences.
user:
TOPIC: why do we get goosebumps when we are cold or scared
SPINE: Why it happens — Explain the real cause behind a thing people experience but misunderstand.
TONE: plain, spoken, confident
VOICE RATE: 1x   ASPECT: 16:9   TARGET LENGTH: 12s

Write exactly 5 scenes, one per beat, in this order:
  1. The question — Open on the exact thing the viewer notices and quietly asks "why?". (default shot: hero)
  2. The guess — State the common, intuitive explanation people reach for. (default shot: f1)
  3. The real mechanism — Name the actual mechanism in one plain, spoken sentence. (default shot: f2)
  4. The proof — Give one concrete example or test that shows the mechanism is real. (default shot: f4)
  5. The takeaway — Land the single idea the viewer should remember. (default shot: s6)

Size each scene's narration to about 6 words so the whole script lands near 12s.
Use only these frame ids for art: hero, f1, f2, f4, s6 (you may reassign among them, but keep them distinct across scenes).

Return JSON matching this schema:
